properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 15 at 7:47PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 747 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 9
miles northwest of Haswell, or 41 miles north of North La Junta,
moving east at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Haswell.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued August 15 at 7:43PM MDT until August 15 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Rural and low lying areas along Bijou Creek in central
Adams and southwestern Morgan Counties.

* WHEN...Until 900 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying along Bijou creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 739 PM MDT, Local law enforcement reported flooding had
occurred along Bijou Creek through Adams County. Water had caused
closer of a couple county roads, but they have since reopened.
Water had also crested and spilled onto Colfax Avenue in rural
Adams County. The crest has passed this area, but will continue
moving downstream and affect areas farther north through the Hoyt
area and toward the confluence with the South Platte River in
Morgan County.

- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Bijou Creek.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
rural and low lying areas along Bijou Creek.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 15 at 7:17PM MDT until August 15 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of east central and northeast Colorado, including
eastern Elbert, Lincoln, Washington, Sedgwick, and Phillips
Counties.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Additional thunderstorms and heavy rainfall this evening,
combined with the heavy rainfall from the past 3 days, will bring
a threat for flash flooding this afternoon and evening. Stronger
storms will be capable of producing 1 to 2 inches of rain in 30
minutes, with isolated areas receiving storm totals of 3+ inches.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued August 15 at 4:59PM MDT until August 15 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
continue to be possible over the Aspen Acres burn scar.

* WHERE...Aspen Acres Burn Scar

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Aspen Acres burn scar is expected
up to and during the period of the watch. Residents near the Aspen
Acres burn scar should prepare for potential debris flow. Be sure
to stay up to date with information from local authorities. Heavy
rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas, street
flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting
thunderstorms with heavy rainfall over the burn scar, which may
lead to flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Beulah, San Isabel, and highways 165 and 78 in and around the
Aspen Acres Burn Scar.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 15 at 11:32AM MDT until August 16 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of east central Colorado, including the following
area, Cheyenne CO and west central Kansas, including the following
areas, Gove, Greeley, Logan, Wallace and Wichita.

* WHEN...From 6 PM MDT  /7 PM CDT/ this evening through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1-3 inches of rain the past couple nights along with the
potential for another cluster or two of storms this evening and
overnight increases the potential for some flooding and even
flash flooding. Rainfall rates of 1.5 to 2.5 inches per hour is
possible in the strongest cells.
